subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw design a Gateway-side credential forwarding flow?
rationale: Both paths change a sensitive provider credential boundary, and automation should not decide whether node hosts may acquire and transfer Gateway-owned OAuth material without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable Gateway-host instruction while preserving loopback or tunnel semantics.

options.title: Forward credentials to the Gateway
options.body: Design an authenticated Gateway RPC or setup flow that stores provider auth material on the Gateway without consuming tokens locally first.

options.title: Warn but preserve permissive login
options.body: Keep the local write path with a warning, accepting the wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable Gateway-host instruction while preserving loopback or tunnel semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored the closed maintainer draft for this exact remote-node OAuth guard and has recent related auth repair history.
